note: Initial rubric from the build prompt sections 5a-5c. Anchors cite the deal memos (Deal_Memos.pdf) and partner meeting notes.

G1.name: Stage and cheque fit
G1.rule: Pre-seed or seed, first institutional round, sensible valuation (roughly a $100K-$500K cheque).

G2.name: Regulatory existence risk
G2.rule: Existence depends on a favourable regulatory change, or a single rule change would hit the business directly (R6, Coinlane).

G3.name: Portfolio conflict
G3.rule: Semantic match of one-liner and product against every portfolio row. Always flag; a false alarm beats a miss (Meeting 4).

G4.name: Integrity
G4.rule: Deck and form contradict each other, credentials are inflated, or numbers do not reconcile. Ask for the numbers; never allege.

C1.name: Founder-market fit
C1.covers: Earned secrets, skills fit, time spent on this problem.

anchors.0: Pedigree with no link to this problem or customer. Credentials are the whole case (Meeting 3: AeroDrop scored 7.5 on credentials; 'credentials are not a business').
anchors.3: Relevant adjacent skill but no earned insight and a gap the founder does not see (Petalry: strong marketer, never owned a P&L, 'unaware of the gap').
anchors.5: Skills fit the problem and some time spent on it; one or two specific insights, not yet tested in the field.
anchors.7: Months in the field with customers, describes what they actually want in their words (SuperK: months in small-town stores; Wint: sat across the table from the customer first).
anchors.10: Years on a hard problem; answers 'what would make you quit?' with a specific technical or commercial milestone (ePlane).

anchors.0: Says the hardest risk is someone else's problem (CampusCredit: defaults are 'something the NBFC partner handles').
anchors.3: Acknowledges the risk with no plan (AeroDrop: regulation and liability 'solved once the tech works').
anchors.5: Names the risk and a plausible mitigation.
anchors.7: Owns the risk with a concrete milestone sequence (ePlane: long regulatory path, clear milestone sequence).
anchors.10: Has already absorbed and managed the risk in the field (Jai Kisan: registered and assessed thousands of farmers before lending).

C3.name: Quality of customer pull
C3.covers: Repeat, conversion, groundwork. Not raw size.

anchors.0: No paying or committed customer and no groundwork (AeroDrop: no signed customer).
anchors.3: Top-line growth, downloads or followers with no retention data, or growth bought through paid channels (Prepnest: no 30/90-day numbers; Petalry: two thirds of orders from paid social, repeat not tracked).
anchors.5: Paying customers and early repeat or conversion signals, partly from one channel or one town.
anchors.7: Product in live use with measured conversion or cohort repeat (Unbox: live sites, pilots treated as learning; Giva: repeat by cohort).
anchors.10: Customer groundwork before the product, plus measured repeat or conversion by cohort (Jai Kisan: thousands registered first; SuperK: dozens of stores visited).

C4.name: Fluency and honesty with the numbers
C4.covers: Cohorts, CAC by channel, figures that reconcile.

anchors.0: Key numbers contradict across deck and form, or credentials and metrics are inflated (G4 pattern).
anchors.3: Answers with channel-level averages; the deciding number is missing (Petalry: no repeat rate; Meeting 1 'a missing number should drag the score').
anchors.5: Core numbers present and mostly consistent; one important number not measured.
anchors.7: CAC by channel, cohort data and unit economics that reconcile in code.
anchors.10: Cohort repeat, gross margin and CAC by channel without notes, and they reconcile (Giva).

C5.name: Fits a pre-seed cheque
C5.covers: Capital intensity, valuation, path to the next round.

anchors.0: Later-stage round or a model that only works with far more capital than the fund deploys (HopBox: 'pass on structure, not people').
anchors.3: Capital-intensive; the path to the next round depends on a large raise to reach density or scale.
anchors.5: Moderate capital needs; the next round is plausible if stated milestones are hit.
anchors.7: This cheque funds clear milestones and a slow path does not force a bad financing (ePlane: cheque sized for a slow regulatory path).
anchors.10: Capital-light, positive contribution, and this round clearly reaches a priced next round.

C6.name: Why now, and what happens when someone copies it
C6.covers: What changed in the world; defensibility.

anchors.0: No why-now, and the founder gets defensive about copying (Prepnest: bristled at the copy question; R8).
anchors.3: Generic why-now ('market is growing'); copying not considered.
anchors.5: A specific change that makes this possible now and a plausible but untested moat.
anchors.7: Why-now tied to a real change, plus something hard to copy (SuperK: franchise-style model with real field execution).
anchors.10: A real change plus an earned advantage that compounds, with a considered answer to a well-funded copier.

deeptech.question: Is there a milestone path through regulators and customers?

missing_evidence.rule: R4: a missing number lowers the score; it is never skipped. The gap is listed by name.

requires: confidence med or higher on C1, C2, C3
